🔗 https://t.co/ztLlfcFM66…

🔗 https://t.co/a3t5Yif5oc

title_en:
If I was 22 and broke, I'd do this TONIGHT:

> learn GTM engineering in 30 days
> pick one type of B2B company
> map every company in their market
> book them sales calls with AI
> charge $3K a month per company
> hit $10K months inside 6 months
> quit your job
> move into your own place
> book the trip you keep putting off

Here's EXACTLY how to do the first six:

0. WHAT THE JOB IS (30 SECONDS)

Every B2B company needs a steady flow of new customers.

Plenty of them still rely on referrals and whoever the founder knows.

A GTM engineer builds the system that finds every company that could buy and books sales calls with them.

The title barely existed before 2024, and job postings for it grew 205% in a year.

Vercel and OpenAI pay $250K+ for it, and the median salary sits at $127.5K.

You can sell the same work straight to companies and skip the job application.

1. LEARN THE STACK (30 DAYS)

Spend week one on who buys and why, before you open a single tool.

Then learn 4 tools and ignore everything else for now.

Clay is where the lists get built, and Claude Code handles the research and first drafts.

Add n8n to move replies into Slack and the CRM, and EmailBison to send.

2. PICK ONE TYPE OF COMPANY (ONE WEEKEND)

Their customers need to be worth $10K+ each.

The market has to hold 50,000+ companies, and under 10,000 you're better off going account by account.

And somebody on their side has to take the calls you book.

Boring industries are the easiest to start in.

A building contractor's inbox has a supplier invoice in it and not much else, so your email gets read.

3. MAP THEIR WHOLE MARKET (ONE WEEK, $0 TO START)

Pull companies from Apollo's free plan and Google Maps, then stack industry directories on top.

Have AI read every company's website and score it against the client's best customers.

Tell it what a bad fit looks like too, and cut anything under 80%.

Find the emails with a waterfall: Icypeas → Prospeo → LeadMagic, with BlitzAPI for phone numbers

Then verify everything with MillionVerifier and run the catch-alls through BounceBan.

We mapped 69,204 businesses off Google Maps for one client, and it booked them 53 meetings in 50 days.

4. SET UP SENDING (14 DAYS)

Buy secondary domains on Porkbun, and never send from the client's real one.

Get inboxes from ScaledMail with SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every domain.

Warm them for 14 days before a single cold email goes out.

Cap each inbox at 15 cold emails a day and turn open tracking off.

When you need more volume, add inboxes instead of pushing the ones you have.

5. WRITE THE EMAIL (ONE AFTERNOON)

Keep it under 65 words, and under 40 if it's going to an Outlook inbox.

Open with one real detail about their business.

Our AI-written first lines hit a 0.27% reply rate.

A campaign that used the prospect's own project and location hit 14.5%.

Close on something free they can say yes to, like a sample list or a mockup of their own work.

Give every version 1,000+ sends before you decide it doesn't work.

6. CATCH EVERY REPLY (SAME DAY)

Build an n8n flow that tags each reply by intent and posts the good ones into Slack.

Answer inside a minute, then pick up the phone and call them.

Contacting a lead within a minute lifts conversions by 391% (Velocify).

Offer 2 times inside the next 2 days ("Tuesday at 11 or Wednesday at 2?") instead of sending a calendar link.

Judge every campaign on contacts per lead: under 500 is good, around 1,000 needs a tweak, and 2,000+ means the offer's wrong.

Run the numbers at $3K a month:

1 client = $3K
4 clients = $12K
10 clients = $30K

GTM engineering is where data science was in 2012.

The people who'll regret missing it are sitting in SDR seats right now.

Nobody has ever needed a tutorial on quitting their job.

Our Head of GTM wrote a 40-page guide on every part of GTM engineering.

Comment "GTM" and I'll send it over (must be following)

full_text_zh:
如果我 22 岁并且破产了，我今晚会这样做：

> 30天学会GTM工程
> 选择一种类型的 B2B 公司
> 绘制市场中每家公司的地图
> 使用 AI 为他们预约销售电话
> 每家公司每月收费 3,000 美元
> 在 6 个月内达到每月 1 万美元
> 辞职
> 搬到你自己的地方
> 预订您一直推迟的旅行

以下是前六项具体操作方法：

0. 工作是什么（30 秒）

每个 B2B 公司都需要源源不断的新客户。

他们中的许多人仍然依赖推荐和创始人认识的人。

GTM 工程师构建了一个系统，该系统可以找到每家可以购买的公司并与其预约销售电话。

这个头衔在 2024 年之前几乎不存在，并且该职位的招聘信息在一年内增长了 205%。

Vercel 和 OpenAI 为此支付了 25 万美元以上，薪资中位数为 12.75 万美元。

您可以直接向公司出售相同的工作并跳过工作申请。

1.学习堆栈（30天）

在打开单个工具之前，先花第一周的时间了解谁购买以及购买原因。

然后学习 4 个工具，暂时忽略其他一切。

Clay 是构建列表的地方，Claude Code 负责研究和初稿。

添加 n8n 将回复移动到 Slack 和 CRM 中，并添加 EmailBison 进行发送。

2. 选择一种类型的公司（一个周末）

他们的客户每个价值需要超过 1 万美元。

市场必须容纳 50,000 家以上的公司，而 10,000 家以下的公司最好逐个账户进行分析。

他们这边必须有人接听您预订的电话。

无聊的行业是最容易起步的。

建筑承包商的收件箱中只有供应商发票，没有其他内容，因此您的电子邮件会被阅读。

3. 绘制整个市场地图（一周，0 美元开始）

从 Apollo 的免费计划和 Google 地图中提取公司，然后将行业目录堆叠在顶部。

让人工智能阅读每家公司的网站，并根据客户的最佳客户对其进行评分。

告诉它什么是不合适的，并将任何东西减少到 80% 以下。

找到瀑布电子邮件：Icypeas→Prospeo→LeadMagic，与BlitzAPI的电话号码

然后使用 MillionVerifier 验证所有内容并通过 BounceBan 运行所有内容。

我们为一位客户在 Google 地图上绘制了 69,204 家企业的地图，并在 50 天内为他们预订了 53 场会议。

4. 设置发送（14 天）

在 Porkbun 上购买二级域名，并且永远不要从客户的真实域名发送。

在每个域上使用 SPF、DKIM 和 DMARC 从 ScaledMail 获取收件箱。

在发出一封冰冷的电子邮件之前，先将它们加热 14 天。

将每个收件箱每天最多发送 15 封冷电子邮件，并关闭开放式跟踪。

当您需要更多容量时，请添加收件箱，而不是推送现有的收件箱。

5. 写电子邮件（一个下午）

将其控制在 65 个字以下，如果要发送到 Outlook 收件箱，则控制在 40 个字以下。

首先介绍有关其业务的一个真实细节。

我们人工智能编写的第一行回复率达到了 0.27%。

使用潜在客户自己的项目和地点的活动达到了 14.5%。

接近他们可以接受的免费东西，比如样本列表或他们自己作品的模型。

在您确定每个版本不起作用之前，请先发送 1,000 多次。

6. 收到每条回复（同一天）

构建一个 n8n 流程，按意图标记每个回复并将好的回复发布到 Slack 中。

一分钟内回答，然后拿起电话给他们打电话。

一分钟内联系潜在客户可将转化率提高 391% (Velocify)。

在接下来的 2 天内提供 2 次优惠（“星期二 11 点还是星期三 2 点？”），而不是发送日历链接。

根据每个潜在客户的联系人来判断每个营销活动：低于 500 名就很好，大约 1,000 名需要调整，超过 2,000 名则意味着报价错误。

计算每月 3K 美元的数字：

1 个客户 = 3,000 美元
4 个客户 = 12,000 美元
10 个客户 = 3 万美元

GTM 工程相当于 2012 年数据科学的地位。

那些会后悔错过它的人现在就坐在特别提款权席位上。

没有人需要关于辞职的教程。

我们的 GTM 负责人针对 GTM 工程的各个部分编写了 40 页的指南。

title:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams
title_en:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot were all affected by the same outage. Different services, but they still depended on the same company's infrastructure.

Acurast points out something interesting here.

Instead of running everything in one cloud, developers can spread their workloads across phones in different countries. If one phone goes offline, other phones running the same workload can keep working.

Their network now has over 360,000 phones across 175+ countries, according to the latest blog.

But I think there's an important difference.

Acurast can't magically fix Outlook when Microsoft's servers go down. And an AI agent that needs Outlook's API would still have problems.

What it can do is help keep independent tasks running, like monitoring services or sending alerts through another system.

I'd actually like to see Acurast test this in public. Take one Processor offline while a real application is running and show how the network handles it.

That would tell us more about reliability than just counting connected phones.

full_text_en:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Acurast points out something interesting here.

Instead of running everything in one cloud, developers can spread their workloads across phones in different countries. If one phone goes offline, other phones running the same workload can keep working.

Their network now has over 360,000 phones across 175+ countries, according to the latest blog.

But I think there's an important difference.

Acurast can't magically fix Outlook when Microsoft's servers go down. And an AI agent that needs Outlook's API would still have problems.

What it can do is help keep independent tasks running, like monitoring services or sending alerts through another system.

I'd actually like to see Acurast test this in public. Take one Processor offline while a real application is running and show how the network handles it.

That would tell us more about reliability than just counting connected phones.
full_text_zh:
11 月 12 日，我正在阅读 @Acurast 关于 Microsoft 宕机事件的新帖子，其中一个内容引起了我的思考。

Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 均受到同一故障的影响。不同的服务，但它们仍然依赖于同一家公司的基础设施。

阿库拉斯特在这里指出了一些有趣的事情。

开发人员可以将工作负载分散到不同国家/地区的手机上，而不是在一个云中运行所有内容。如果一部电话离线，运行相同工作负载的其他电话可以继续工作。

根据最新博客，他们的网络目前在 175 多个国家/地区拥有超过 360,000 部电话。

但我认为有一个重要的区别。

当 Microsoft 的服务器出现故障时，Acurast 无法神奇地修复 Outlook。而需要 Outlook API 的 AI 代理仍然会遇到问题。

它可以做的是帮助保持独立任务的运行，例如监控服务或通过另一个系统发送警报。

我实际上希望看到 Acurast 公开测试这一点。在实际应用程序运行时使一个处理器离线并显示网络如何处理它。

这将告诉我们更多关于可靠性的信息，而不仅仅是计算连接的电话。

title:
“Delivered” can start an argument as easily as end one.

Imagine an agent ordering steel for a project. The shipment arr
title_en:
“Delivered” can start an argument as easily as end one.

Imagine an agent ordering steel for a project. The shipment arrives. The buyer disputes whether it meets the specification.

Both agents have a reason to say they’re right. Who settles it?

That’s the lens I’m using for @GenLayer move to the @arbitrum stack.

The GenLayer Chain moved from ZK Stack to Nitro. It hosts the consensus contracts that track who judges a case, their votes, appeals and the final outcome.

The method of judgment stays the same. Validators running different AI models reach agreement through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent contracts still execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

My take: the rules for resolving a disagreement should survive a change in the infrastructure recording it. GenLayer preserved that boundary while moving its chain to a stack with years of production use.

For anyone building agents that spend money, here’s a question worth answering before the first purchase:

What would your agent need to see before accepting “job done”?

两位经纪人都有理由说他们是对的。谁来解决？

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum

That’s the lens I’m using for @GenLayer move to the @arbitrum stack.

The GenLayer Chain moved from ZK Stack to Nitro. It hosts the consensus contracts that track who judges a case, their votes, appeals and the final outcome.

The method of judgment stays the same. Validators running different AI models reach agreement through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent contracts still execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

My take: the rules for resolving a disagreement should survive a change in the infrastructure recording it. GenLayer preserved that boundary while moving its chain to a stack with years of production use.

想象一下一个代理商为一个项目订购钢材。货物到达。买方对是否符合规格提出异议。

两位经纪人都有理由说他们是对的。谁来解决？

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum 堆栈的镜头。

GenLayer 链从 ZK Stack 迁移到 Nitro。它托管共识合约，跟踪案件的法官、他们的投票、上诉和最终结果。

判断方法保持不变。运行不同人工智能模型的验证者通过乐观民主达成一致。智能合约仍在验证器节点上的 GenVM 中执行。

我的看法是：解决分歧的规则应该在记录分歧的基础设施发生变化后继续存在。 GenLayer 保留了这一边界，同时将其链转移到具有多年生产使用的堆栈中。

对于任何花钱的建筑代理商来说，在第一次购买之前，有一个值得回答的问题：

在接受“工作完成”之前，您的代理人需要看到什么？

Its c
title_en:
A court does not run its own power grid. GenLayer, the adjudication layer for AI agents, follows a similar split.

Its chain moved to Arbitrum Nitro, the same software behind the chain Robinhood launched in July.

That chain is operated with Conduit, a company whose whole business is running chains, with more than 60 mainnets on its platform. The GenLayer team keeps its hands on the protocol.

I like that division of labour. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts are where GenLayer's judgment lives, and the move leaves them as they were. Validators keep the same role, and their nodes now connect to the new chain.

The next phase of the Bradbury testnet went live the same day. The work with ZKsync continues on Prividium and enterprise, while the public network is the part that moved.

@GenLayer chose a stack that others already run on, and @arbitrum is where many of the builders it wants to work with already are.

Would you rather a protocol team run its own chain, or leave that part to specialists?

布拉德伯里测试网的下一阶段于同一天上线。 ZKsync 的工作在 Prividium 和企业上继续进行，而公共网络是移动的部分。

@GenLayer 选择了其他人已经运行的堆栈，而 @arbitrum 是它想要使用的许多构建器已经所在的位置。

𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗜𝗔𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗠 𝗧𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗦 𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗥𝗬 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧

What actually happens inside an AI agent?

An AI agent is more than an LLM connected to a prompt. It follows a continuous workflow where it receives information, reasons, accesses memory, plans tasks, and executes actions.

Here's a breakdown of the architecture behind modern AI agents.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 & 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

The starting point where an agent receives and understands incoming information.

→ User text and instructions

→ API calls

→ Sensor data

→ Events and triggers

02 — 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗜𝗡𝗘 / 𝗟𝗟𝗠

The brain of the agent that analyzes information and decides what to do next.

→ Chain-of-Thought

→ ReAct

→ Plan-and-Execute

→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

Allows agents to retain information and maintain context across tasks.

→ Short-term: Conversation context and working state.

→ Long-term: Vector stores and episodic memory.

→ Learned patterns: Previously stored information.

04 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗘

Breaks complex goals into smaller tasks and organizes their execution.

→ Goal decomposition

→ Task sequencing

→ Step-by-step execution

→ Progress tracking

Example:

→ Step 1: Understand the goal.

→ Step 2: Break it into subtasks.

→ Step 3: Execute each step.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 / 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

This is where agents interact with external systems and perform real actions.

→ Model Context Protocol (MCP)

→ API calls

→ Code execution

→ Database queries

→ File system

→ External services like GitHub

Results are sent back to the reasoning engine for further processing.

06 — 𝗚𝗨𝗔𝗥𝗗𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦 & 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬

Keeps agent operations within defined security boundaries.

→ Permission controls

→ Approval gates

→ Content filtering

→ Rate limits

→ Human-in-the-loop checkpoints

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Monitors agent activities and helps developers maintain system reliability.

→ Execution tracing

→ Error monitoring

→ Workflow tracking

→ Performance monitoring

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗙𝗟𝗢𝗪:

Input
↓
Perception
↓
Reasoning + Memory
↓
Can the agent answer directly?

→ YES: Generate output.

→ NO: Move to planning and tool execution.

Planning
↓
Tool Execution
↓
Results
↓
Goal Evaluation
↓
Final Output

If the goal isn't achieved, the agent returns to reasoning and planning to continue the task.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

An AI agent isn't just a language model. It's a complete system where reasoning, memory, planning, tools, safety, and monitoring work together.

Understanding this architecture is the first step toward building AI agents that can actually complete real-world tasks.

𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗜𝗔𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗠 𝗧𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗦 𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗥𝗬 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧

人工智能代理内部到底发生了什么？

AI 代理不仅仅是连接到提示的法学硕士。它遵循连续的工作流程，接收信息、推理、访问内存、计划任务并执行操作。

以下是现代人工智能代理背后的架构细分。

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 & 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

代理接收并理解传入信息的起点。

→ 用户文本和说明

→ API 调用

→ 传感器数据

→ 事件和触发器

02 — 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗜𝗡𝗘 / 𝗟𝗟𝗠

智能体的大脑，负责分析信息并决定下一步该做什么。

→ 思想链

→ 反应

→ 计划与执行

→ 决策

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

允许代理保留信息并维护跨任务的上下文。

→ 短期：对话情境和工作状态。

→ 长期：向量存储和情景记忆。

→ 学习模式：之前存储的信息。

04 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗘

将复杂的目标分解为较小的任务并组织其执行。

→ 目标分解

→ 任务排序

→ 逐步执行

→ 进度追踪

例子：

→ 第 1 步：了解目标。

→ 第 2 步：将其分解为子任务。

→ 步骤3：执行每一步。

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 / 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

这是代理与外部系统交互并执行实际操作的地方。

→ 模型上下文协议 (MCP)

→ API 调用

→ 代码执行

→ 数据库查询

→ 文件系统

→ GitHub 等外部服务

结果被发送回推理引擎进行进一步处理。

06 — 𝗚𝗨𝗔𝗥𝗗𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦 & 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬

将代理操作保持在定义的安全边界内。

→ 权限控制

→ 审批门

→ 内容过滤

→ 速率限制

→ 人机交互检查点

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

监控代理活动并帮助开发人员维护系统可靠性。

→ 执行追踪

→ 错误监控

→ 工作流程跟踪

→ 性能监控

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗙𝗟𝗢𝗪:

输入
↓
感知
↓
推理+记忆
↓
代理可以直接回答吗？

→ 是：生成输出。

→ 否：转向规划和工具执行。

规划
↓
工具执行
↓
结果
↓
目标评估
↓
最终输出

如果目标没有实现，智能体将返回推理并计划继续执行任务。

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

人工智能代理不仅仅是一个语言模型。这是一个完整的系统，推理、记忆、规划、工具、安全和监控协同工作。

了解这种架构是构建能够真正完成现实世界任务的人工智能代理的第一步。

关注@AamirAnsar94694 了解更多人工智能工具和技术更新。

title_en:
Why would GenLayer run on two paths at once?

Picture two customers walking in on the same day.

The first is a small team building an AI agent app. They want a public network, open tooling and builders already nearby. For them, GenLayer's public network now runs on the @arbitrum stack. Nitro is built around Geth, so normal Ethereum tools work as they are. Robinhood runs its own chain on the same software.

The second is a group of banks. They want to settle contracts between themselves, and that cannot sit on a public chain. For them, @GenLayer keeps working with Matter Labs on Prividium, a private, permissioned version.

Two different needs, same engine. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts work the same way. What changed was only where the contracts touch the chain: the bridge, the Ethereum link and gas handling.

So the move does not shrink the plan. It gives each customer the right door. And Bradbury going live on the new stack the same day shows it is already running.

Which door do you think brings in more builders first, public or private?

full_text_en:
Why would GenLayer run on two paths at once?

Picture two customers walking in on the same day.

The first is a small team building an AI agent app. They want a public network, open tooling and builders already nearby. For them, GenLayer's public network now runs on the @arbitrum stack. Nitro is built around Geth, so normal Ethereum tools work as they are. Robinhood runs its own chain on the same software.

The second is a group of banks. They want to settle contracts between themselves, and that cannot sit on a public chain. For them, @GenLayer keeps working with Matter Labs on Prividium, a private, permissioned version.

Two different needs, same engine. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts work the same way. What changed was only where the contracts touch the chain: the bridge, the Ethereum link and gas handling.

So the move does not shrink the plan. It gives each customer the right door. And Bradbury going live on the new stack the same day shows it is already running.

Which door do you think brings in more builders first, public or private?
full_text_zh:
为什么 GenLayer 会同时在两条路径上运行？

想象一下同一天走进来的两个顾客。

第一个是一个构建人工智能代理应用程序的小团队。他们想要一个公共网络、开放工具和已经在附近的构建器。对于他们来说，GenLayer 的公共网络现在在 @arbitrum 堆栈上运行。 Nitro 是围绕 Geth 构建的，因此普通的以太坊工具可以按原样工作。 Robinhood 在同一软件上运行自己的链。

第二个是银行集团。他们想要在彼此之间结算合同，而这不能放在公共链上。对于他们来说，@GenLayer 继续与 Matter Labs 合作开发 Prividium（一个私有的、经过许可的版本）。

两种不同的需求，相同的引擎。乐观民主、GenVM 和智能合约的工作原理是一样的。改变的只是合约接触链的地方：桥、以太坊链接和天然气处理。

因此此举并没有缩小计划。它为每个客户提供了正确的大门。 Bradbury 于同一天在新堆栈上上线，表明它已经在运行。

您认为哪扇门首先会吸引更多的建筑商，是公共的还是私人的？

Developer ILFforever
title_en:
👻 YO-KAI WATCH 4++ RECOMPILATION brings 4K, ultrawide, high FPS and native Linux support to PC! 🎮🔥

Developer ILFforever is bringing Level-5's Nintendo Switch action RPG to Windows and Linux through static recompilation, translating the original ARM64 game code into a native PC application with a Vulkan graphics renderer!

🔥 FEATURES:

✅ NATIVE WINDOWS & LINUX! Including a Linux AppImage launcher — no Switch emulator required!

✅ 4K & ULTRAWIDE! Supports 1080p, 1440p, 4K and 21:9/32:9 aspect ratios!

✅ HIGH FRAME RATES! 30, 60, 120, 144 FPS and uncapped options!

✅ DLSS & FSR! Upscaling and frame generation for smoother presentation, with platform-specific support!

✅ ENHANCED GRAPHICS! PCSS soft shadows, improved anti-aliasing, TAA, SMAA and sharper textures!

✅ MOD SUPPORT! Includes compatibility with the fan-made English translation patch!

✅ MODERN CONTROLS! Keyboard, mouse, Xbox, PlayStation and Joy-Con controllers, with configurable bindings and vibration!

✅ DEDICATED LAUNCHER! Import your own game files, build the PC version, manage updates, saves, DLC and mods!

🔥 BETA v1.5.0 — PLAYABLE BUT UNFINISHED!

The opening, several locations and late-game battles have been tested. However, most of the story remains unverified, so crashes and missing graphical effects are possible.

💿 Requires your own Yo-kai Watch 4++ Nintendo Switch game files, updated to version 2.2.0.

🛠️ Developed by ILFforever, with extensive AI-assisted programming using Claude Code.

✅ 4K 和超宽！支持 1080p、1440p、4K 和 21:9/32:9 宽高比！

✅ 高帧率！ 30、60、120、144 FPS 和无上限选项！

✅ DLSS 和 FSR！升级和帧生成可实现更流畅的演示，并提供特定于平台的支持！

✅ 增强的图形！ PCSS 柔和阴影、改进的抗锯齿、TAA、SMAA 和更清晰的纹理！

✅ 模组支持！包括与粉丝制作的英文翻译补丁的兼容性！

✅ 现代控制！键盘、鼠标、Xbox、PlayStation 和 Joy-Con 控制器，具有可配置的绑定和振动！

✅ 专用发射器！导入您自己的游戏文件、构建 PC 版本、管理更新、保存、DLC 和模组！

🔥 BETA v1.5.0 — 可玩但未完成！

开局、多个地点和游戏后期的战斗都经过了测试。然而，故事的大部分内容仍未得到验证，因此可能会出现崩溃和图形效果缺失的情况。

title:
something people might overlook when using AI agents for trading is the paperwork that comes after every transaction.

@
title_en:
something people might overlook when using AI agents for trading is the paperwork that comes after every transaction.

@meetmotes is exploring autonomous agents for financial markets, but i think there's another part of the experience worth discussing.

imagine an agent making trades across different markets throughout the week.

after some time, how easily can the user find out what happened?

which asset was bought or sold, when the transaction happened, what price was executed, how much was paid in fees, and what the final position looks like.

these details matter when reviewing performance, tracking a portfolio, or preparing financial records.

i wouldn't want users to dig through dozens of transaction links just to understand what their own agent has been doing.

a clear, downloadable activity history could make a big difference.

automation should save users time, not create another administrative headache.

a good AI agent should make the activity easier to manage, even after the trade is finished.

想象一下一个代理在一周内跨不同市场进行交易。

一段时间后，用户如何容易地发现发生了什么？

购买或出售哪些资产、交易何时发生、执行价格是多少、支付了多少费用以及最终头寸是什么样的。

在审查绩效、跟踪投资组合或准备财务记录时，这些细节很重要。

我不希望用户挖掘数十个交易链接只是为了了解他们自己的代理一直在做什么。

清晰、可下载的活动历史记录可能会产生很大的影响。

自动化应该节省用户时间，而不是造成另一个管理难题。

一个好的人工智能代理应该使活动更容易管理，即使在交易完成后也是如此。

title:
Here's how hackers are now using AI to attack companies, according to a new Google report:

1. A software company releas
title_en:
Here's how hackers are now using AI to attack companies, according to a new Google report:

1. A software company releases a security update

2. An AI agent compares the old code to the new code

3. It figures out exactly which weakness was just fixed

4. It writes an attack for that weakness

5. It hits every company that hasn't installed the update yet

No human needed at any step.

Google found one of these tools, called "exploit_agent," sitting on an exposed hacker server.

Its verdict: "The era of autonomous attacks has arrived."
title_zh:
根据谷歌的一份新报告，黑客现在如何利用人工智能来攻击公司：

1.某软件公司发布安全更新

2. AI 代理将旧代码与新代码进行比较

3.它准确地指出哪个弱点刚刚被修复

4. 针对该弱点编写攻击

5.它会影响所有尚未安装更新的公司

someone just reverse engineered Apple Watch

you can now control Claude Code from your wrist

see term
title_en:
this is crazy...

someone just reverse engineered Apple Watch

you can now control Claude Code from your wrist

see terminal output, approve permissions, and send voice commands

Claude keeps coding on your Mac, and every time it wants to edit a file or run a command, your wrist buzzes and you tap approve or deny

setup takes about 10 minutes:

1. on the watch turn off Private Wi-Fi Address for your network, the app finds your Mac through Bonjour
2. git clone the repo, then cd skill/bridge && npm install
3. run ./skill/setup-hooks.sh from the repo root to add the Claude Code hooks
4. start the bridge with node server.js and grab the 6-digit code
5. cd ios/ClaudeWatch, run xcodegen generate, set your team on both targets and run them from Xcode
6. enter the code on the iPhone, start Claude Code in a new terminal

try it today:
https://t.co/9Tnj3OzxN6

title:
Final grade. Wrong number. Zero alerts.

I found it when I checked my result against my own records. The score was lower
title_en:
Final grade. Wrong number. Zero alerts.

I found it when I checked my result against my own records. The score was lower than I had calculated. I went through each mark, found the gap and asked my lecturer for the full breakdown. One record had been omitted. It was corrected.

What it left me with: a result means nothing if the process behind it stays hidden.

That stays with me every time I look at @GenLayer moving its coordination chain to @arbitrum.

GenLayer adjudicates for the agentic economy. AI validators running distinct models dispute judgment calls and converge through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent Contracts execute in GenVM. Moving to Arbitrum Nitro positions that layer where many of the builders who will need it are already operating.

What relocated to Nitro, operated by Conduit:

- Sequencing, committee formation, vote tallies, appeals and staked resolutions
- Bridge mechanics, Ethereum interface handling and gas accounting

What stayed fully intact:

- Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and Intelligent Contracts
- Validator nodes reconnected to the new chain; their function unchanged

Proximity is a condition for adoption, not proof of it.

If an AI agent made a call that affected something real for you, what would make you trust it without checking yourself: an auditable validator record, evidence the outcome was contested, or an on-chain dispute you could trigger?
title_zh:
最终成绩。号码错误。零警报。

当我根据自己的记录检查结果时，我发现了这一点。分数比我计算的要低。我检查了每个分数，找到了差距，并向我的讲师询问了完整的细目。遗漏了一项记录。已更正。

它给我留下的印象是：如果结果背后的过程保持隐藏，那么结
full_text_en:

full_text_zh:
最终成绩。号码错误。零警报。

当我根据自己的记录检查结果时，我发现了这一点。分数比我计算的要低。我检查了每个分数，找到了差距，并向我的讲师询问了完整的细目。遗漏了一项记录。已更正。

它给我留下的印象是：如果结果背后的过程保持隐藏，那么结果就毫无意义。

每当我看到 @GenLayer 将其协调链转移到 @arbitrum 时，我都会想起这一点。

GenLayer 裁决代理经济。运行不同模型的人工智能验证者对判断调用提出争议，并通过乐观民主进行收敛。智能合约在 GenVM 中执行。迁移到 Arbitrum Nitro 后，许多需要它的构建者已经在运行该层。

迁移到 Nitro 并由 Conduit 运营的内容：

- 排序、委员会组建、计票、上诉和质押决议
- 桥梁机制、以太坊接口处理和天然气核算

完好无损的东西：

- 乐观民主、GenVM 和智能合约
- 验证节点重新连接到新链；他们的功能不变

邻近是收养的一个条件，而不是收养的证据。

如果人工智能代理拨打的电话对你来说影响了真实的事情，那么什么会让你在不检查自己的情况下信任它：可审计的验证者记录、结果受到争议的证据，或者你可能引发的链上争议？

title:
I love the idea of an AI agent managing my DeFi portfolio.

But giving it unrestricted access to my wallet?

Yeah, absol
title_en:
I love the idea of an AI agent managing my DeFi portfolio.

But giving it unrestricted access to my wallet?

Yeah, absolutely not. 😂

And apparently, the people building @termix_ai have been thinking about this problem too.

I was going through the AACP whitepaper and found something called Vault Extension.

We have already talked about agents getting hired, completing jobs, and earning USDC.

But managing someone else's money is a completely different story.

Imagine I want an AI agent to manage $2000 across DeFi protocols.

Maybe move liquidity between pools, optimize yield, or rebalance positions when market conditions change.

I want the agent to make decisions.

What I do not want is for it to wake up one morning and send my entire balance to some random address. 💀

This is the problem TermiX wants to address with its StrategyVault and TransactionGuard architecture.

The idea is pretty clever.

Instead of handing an agent control over your wallet, you deposit capital into a dedicated smart contract.

You define the permissions before the job begins.

For example:
→ The agent can interact with approved protocols like Aave or Uniswap.

→ Only specific smart contract functions are permitted.

→ Arbitrary withdrawals and unauthorized transfers are blocked.

→ A stop-loss threshold and execution deadline can be configured.

The agent gets room to execute its strategy, but only within the boundaries you have established.

And the entire transaction history remains onchain.

I particularly like the distinction here.

The agent does not need unrestricted control over your money to do useful work with it.

Of course, smart contract vulnerabilities, bad oracle data, and market crashes are still real risks. Even a well-designed permission system cannot eliminate them.

And Vault Extension is a proposed component of AACP, not something I am treating as a finished production feature.

Still, I think this gives us a glimpse of where TermiX could eventually go.

Today we are discussing AI agents earning $50 for research reports.

Tomorrow, we might be discussing agents managing DAO treasuries, allocating liquidity, and executing financial strategies under programmable restrictions.

That is a much more interesting direction for the agent economy.

I do not need an AI agent that promises to be responsible with my money.

I want infrastructure that limits what it can do when something goes wrong.

That is the part I would like to see TermiX deliver.

full_text_zh:
我喜欢由人工智能代理管理我的 DeFi 投资组合的想法。

但让它不受限制地访问我的钱包？

是的，绝对不是。 😂

显然，构建 @termix_ai 的人们也一直在思考这个问题。

我正在浏览 AACP 白皮书，发现了一个叫做 Vault Extension 的东西。

我们已经讨论过代理被雇用、完成工作和赚取 USDC。

但管理别人的钱是一个完全不同的故事。

想象一下，我想要一个 AI 代理来跨 DeFi 协议管理 2000 美元。

也许可以在资金池之间转移流动性，优化收益率，或者在市场条件发生变化时重新平衡头寸。

我希望代理人做出决定。

我不希望它在一天早上醒来并将我的全部余额发送到某个随机地址。 💀

这就是 TermiX 希望通过其 StrategyVault 和 TransactionGuard 架构解决的问题。

这个想法相当聪明。

您无需将钱包的控制权交给代理，而是将资金存入专用的智能合约。

您可以在作业开始之前定义权限。

例如：
→ 代理可以与 Aave 或 Uniswap 等经批准的协议进行交互。

→ 仅允许特定的智能合约功能。

→ 阻止任意提款和未经授权的转账。

→ 可以配置止损阈值和执行期限。

代理有空间执行其策略，但仅限于您建立的边界内。

整个交易历史记录都保留在链上。

我特别喜欢这里的区别。

代理人不需要对您的资金进行无限制的控制就可以用它来做有用的工作。

当然，智能合约漏洞、不良预言机数据和市场崩溃仍然是真正的风险。即使设计良好的许可系统也无法消除它们。

Vault Extension 是 AACP 提议的组件，而不是我将其视为已完成的生产功能的东西。

尽管如此，我认为这让我们了解了 TermiX 最终的发展方向。

今天我们讨论的是通过研究报告赚取 50 美元的人工智能代理。

明天，我们可能会讨论代理管理 DAO 金库、分配流动性以及在可编程限制下执行财务策略。

对于代理经济来说，这是一个更有趣的方向。

我不需要一个承诺对我的钱负责的人工智能代理。

我希望基础设施能够在出现问题时限制其所能执行的操作。

这就是我希望看到 TermiX 交付的部分。

title:
CUT MY REVERSE ENGINEERING COSTS BY 67% WITH ONE SIMPLE GATE.

I added a confidence gate between Grok and Fable 5.2.

Ou
title_en:
CUT MY REVERSE ENGINEERING COSTS BY 67% WITH ONE SIMPLE GATE.

I added a confidence gate between Grok and Fable 5.2.

Out of 400 tasks, 363 went straight to the cheaper model.

Here's how it works:

→ REA decompiles each function into pseudocode.
→ Grok analyzes it and returns a job, confidence score, and reason for uncertainty.
→ Everything is returned as structured JSON.

The 0.8 threshold decides what happens next.

Above 0.8 → Grok handles it.
Below 0.8 → Fable 5.2 takes over.

The results:

• Grok only: 41 min, $1.80, 19 unknowns.
• Fable only: 26 min, $9.40, 4 unknowns.
• Hybrid: 33 min, $3.10, 5 unknowns.

That's a 67% cost reduction compared with using Fable for everything.

Fable maps inputs, outputs, and side effects while classifying every claim as observation, inference, or unknown.

The smartest part?

Don't send every task to your most expensive model. Let confidence decide when extra intelligence is worth the cost.

Start at 0.8. Adjust the threshold based on which model gets the final call right.

Less waste. Lower costs. Smarter AI workflows.

Would you use this hybrid approach in your own AI pipeline?

full_text_zh:
通过一扇简单的门将我的逆向工程成本降低 67%。

我在 Grok 和 Fable 5.2 之间添加了一个信任门。

在 400 项任务中，有 363 项直接选择了更便宜的模型。

它的工作原理如下：

→ REA 将每个函数反编译为伪代码。
→ Grok 对其进行分析并返回作业、置信度得分以及不确定性的原因。
→ 一切都以结构化 JSON 形式返回。

0.8 阈值决定接下来会发生什么。

高于 0.8 → Grok 可以处理。
低于 0.8 → 寓言 5.2 接管。

结果：

• 仅 Grok：41 分钟，1.80 美元，19 个未知数。
• 仅寓言：26 分钟，9.40 美元，4 个未知数。
• 混合：33 分钟，3.10 美元，5 个未知数。

与一切都使用 Fable 相比，成本降低了 67%。

寓言映射了输入、输出和副作用，同时将每个主张分类为观察、推理或未知。

最聪明的部分？

不要将所有任务都发送给最昂贵的模型。让信心来决定何时值得付出额外的智力代价。

从 0.8 开始。根据哪个模型获得最终正确的结果来调整阈值。

减少浪费。降低成本。更智能的人工智能工作流程。

title_en:
RT @halcyonrayes: i asked claude to implement trellis.2 fully in cuda c++, and it is 5.3x faster than the original pytorch implementation 🚀 

surprisingly, the glb-export function was the bottleneck, not the neural net itself. moving exporting to the gpu gave more gains than anything else.

- zero python runtime, all in c++ ⚡️
- cost 💵 ? ~$7 on claude and ~$60 on compute for testing on h200s through @huggingface jobs

title_en:
I believe trust, accountability, and transparency are the biggest barriers preventing enterprise AI agents from reaching full production. Companies may be impressed by what AI agents can do in demos, but deploying them in real business environments requires much more than good performance.

Businesses need to understand every action an agent takes, why it made certain decisions, and who is responsible if something goes wrong. Without proper monitoring, clear audit trails, and accountability, many companies will hesitate to give AI agents control over important operations.

This is why @Actum_system is addressing an important part of enterprise AI adoption. Making AI agents more transparent, traceable, and accountable could be what helps move them from impressive demos to real-world business use.

#Actum

title: We're getting to the point where AI isn't just answering research questions, it's actually helping carry out the researc
title_en:
We're getting to the point where AI isn't just answering research questions, it's actually helping carry out the research itself.

@DeepPrinciple's Mira Science lets researchers coordinate teams of AI scientists, connect them to professional tools and cloud compute, and run entire research workflows.

that's a pretty big leap from typing a question into ChatGPT and hoping for a good response.

the idea of multiple AI agents working through scientific problems together is pretty crazy when you think about it.

could genuinely change how research gets done over the next few years.
title_zh:
我们已经达到这样的程度：人工智能不仅可以回答研究问题，而且实际上可以帮助开展研究本身。

Junction 2026 is Europe's biggest hackathon: 1
title_en:
We won 🥈 2nd place in the @GetCala partner track at @hackJunction 2026, 

Junction 2026 is Europe's biggest hackathon: 1800+ of builders, 48 hours, and €100,000 in prizes across all its tracks.

I flew from Italy to Finland for one weekend, teamed up with Ignas and Alexander (team: PlayToWin), and in 48 hours we built FlipDD.

the problem: some investors on a founder's meeting list have already backed their competitor, and they'll happily take the meeting just to hear the pitch.

title:
A founder building a court for AI agents learns in the first minute that his interviewer is a lawyer.

Albert Castellana
title_en:
A founder building a court for AI agents learns in the first minute that his interviewer is a lawyer.

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) says: "That's very much on point for this conversation."

Then Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) says something I didn't expect. He gave a TEDx talk around 2017 on the future of regulation and the future of lawyers, and a lot of the legal community criticized him for it.

Now, he says, a lot of what they're discussing is coming through.
That's the part I'd watch.

Being early looks like being wrong for a while. A lawyer said his own profession would change, and the profession pushed back.

Now agents are about to make deals, and the disputes that follow have no obvious court to go to.

My read, and it's only a read: the people best placed to judge whether agents need a different kind of court are the ones who work inside the current one.

The episode opens with a lawyer and a founder discovering they're on the same problem.

@GenLayer's answer is a court where validators, each running a different AI model, judge the dispute.

Who should decide whether agents need their own court: the people who practice law, or the people building the agents?

然后 Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) 说了一些我没想到的话。 2017 年左右，他在 TEDx 上发表了一场关于监管的未来和律师的未来的演讲，许多法律界人士因此批评了他。

他说，现在他们讨论的很多内容都已经实现。
这就是我想看的部分。

早到似乎有一段时间是错误的。一位律师说他自己的职业将会改变，但该职业却退缩了。

现在，代理商即将达成交易，而随之而来的纠纷却没有明显的法庭可诉。

我读过，这只是读过：最有资格判断特工是否需要不同类型法院的人是在当前法院工作的人。

这一集以一位律师和一位创始人发现他们面临同样的问题开始。

@GenLayer 的答案是法庭，每个验证者都运行不同的人工智能模型，对争议进行裁决。

谁应该决定代理人是否需要自己的法庭：是执业律师，还是建立代理人的人？

title:
AI Adoption Requires More Than Intelligent Systems. It Requires Accountability.

As AI agents become part of everyday bu
title_en:
AI Adoption Requires More Than Intelligent Systems. It Requires Accountability.

As AI agents become part of everyday business operations, companies will need more than systems that can complete tasks. They will need to understand exactly how those tasks were carried out.

When an AI agent makes a decision, processes a request or performs an operation, there should be a clear record of what happened, when it happened and who was responsible.

Without that level of visibility, it becomes difficult for businesses to investigate errors, establish responsibility or confidently rely on automated processes.

This is where Actum comes in.

By creating verifiable records of actions across humans, machines and AI agents, @Actum_system provides
  a way to trace activities and establish accountability under predefined rules.

The goal is not simply to make AI more capable, but to make its operations easier to inspect, verify and trust.

Because in business, getting the job done matters. Being able to account for how it was done matters just as much.
#Actum

因为在商业中，完成工作很重要。能够解释它是如何完成的也同样重要。

How does an AI agent find opportunities in the agent economy?

I explored this through @termix_ai and took a closer look at how agents can discover available jobs on https://t.co/cLF8F3gpJK.

One interesting thing is that agents aren’t limited to simply responding to prompts. They can explore job opportunities, review task requirements and find work that matches their capabilities.

This is part of what TermiX is building with AACP: infrastructure that allows AI agents to discover jobs, offer services, collaborate, and participate in an economy where tasks can be completed and payments settled.

There’s still more to explore, but seeing how the job discovery process works gives a better picture of what an agent-powered economy could look like.

AI agents are moving beyond just doing tasks. They’re becoming participants in a marketplace.

That’s the direction TermiX is building towards.

Everyone says AI agents will kill online shopping.

I think they'll just become the shoppers.

Your store is built for people: pictures, a price, a Pay button.

An AI agent can't "see" any of that the way you do. It needs the price and how to pay written in a form it can read.

title: I like the direction @termix_ai is taking: agents are no longer just tools you prompt , they can become buyers and coord
title_en:
I like the direction @termix_ai is taking: agents are no longer just tools you prompt , they can become buyers and coordinate work themselves.

Montage Studio is a good example. You give it a brief, and it writes the treatment and beat-timed shot list. Then it hires three other agents to draw the storyboard, render the shots, and write the song.

After that, it edits everything and delivers a 1080p master.

What stands out to me is that every step is settled in escrow. Agents hiring agents, with the work and payment handled onchain.

This feels like an early look at how AI agents could start operating as real participants in a workflow, not just assistants waiting for instructions.

https://t.co/ovsjww7eJL

title:

but turning that work into a paid service is still a challenge

here’s w
title_en:
AI agents can already write, code, and analyze

but turning that work into a paid service is still a challenge

here’s why that matters 👇

there needs to be a way for people and other agents to find them, hire them, pay for their services, and receive the results

that's the part of the Agent Economy @termix_ai is working on

think of https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB as a marketplace where AI agents can offer services or look for work. behind this marketplace is AACP, the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol that powers the actual commerce workflow

for example, imagine an agent that specializes in writing content. it can publish a service listing with details about what it offers, its price, and delivery time

another agent that needs content can find that service and initiate a transaction. or a buyer can post a request explaining what it needs and let providers submit their offers

AACP connects these discovery paths to the transaction process. once both sides agree on the work and price through an Offer, they move to Checkout. the buyer funds the Order through escrow using stablecoins

an agent can help prepare these transactions, but value-bearing actions still require wallet authorization and signing

and the money isn't simply sent straight to the provider. it's held in a smart contract while the work is being completed

the provider then accepts the funded Order onchain, does the work, and submits the result

the buyer can review the delivery, request a redo, or challenge it if something goes wrong. once the Order reaches settlement, the payment is handled through the contract

that's the workflow TermiX is building around AI agent commerce

and it goes beyond simply creating profiles for agents or helping them find each other. there's an actual process for agreeing on work, funding it, delivering the result, and handling payment

this is an important step toward making AI agents more than just tools that perform tasks

that's what makes TermiX worth watching in the growing agent economy

人们和其他代理需要有一种方法来找到他们、雇用他们、支付他们的服务费用并接收结果

这就是 @termix_ai 正在研究的代理经济

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理已经可以编写、编码和分析

但将这项工作转变为付费服务仍然是一个挑战

这就是为什么这很重要

人们和其他代理需要有一种方法来找到他们、雇用他们、支付他们的服务费用并接收结果

这就是 @termix_ai 正在研究的代理经济的一部分

将 视为人工智能代理可以提供服务或寻找工作的市场。这个市场背后是 AACP，即代理自主商务协议，为实际的商务工作流程提供支持

例如，想象一个专门撰写内容的代理。它可以发布服务列表，其中包含有关其提供的服务、价格和交付时间的详细信息

需要内容的另一个代理可以找到该服务并发起交易。或者买家可以发布请求，解释其需要什么，并让提供商提交他们的报价

AACP 将这些发现路径连接到事务流程。一旦双方通过报价就工作和价格达成一致，他们就会转向结账。买方使用稳定币通过托管为订单提供资金

代理可以帮助准备这些交易，但有价值的操作仍然需要钱包授权和签名

而且钱并不仅仅直接发送给提供商。当工作完成时，它保存在智能合约中

然后，提供商在链上接受资助的订单，完成工作并提交结果

买家可以检查交货情况、请求重做或在出现问题时提出质疑。一旦订单达成结算，付款将通过合同处理

这就是 TermiX 围绕人工智能代理商务构建的工作流程

它不仅仅是为代理商创建个人资料或帮助他们找到彼此。有一个就工作达成一致、为其提供资金、交付结果和处理付款的实际流程

这是使人工智能代理不仅仅是执行任务的工具的重要一步

这就是 TermiX 在不断增长的代理经济中值得关注的原因

title:

On November 12th, the workday for many people around the world
title_en:
This morning brought the first real chill of the season.

On November 12th, the workday for many people around the world came to a sudden halt when Outlook, Teams, and Copilot all stopped responding simultaneously.

This is truly concerning. We implement automation and AI agents to keep our businesses running, yet they often rely on the very same infrastructure, if that infrastructure fails, the agents stop working too.

This is where Acurast offers a different approach. On their network, applications run on individual users' devices rather than on a single company’s servers. Developers can decide how many processors an app should run on and the specific type of hardware to be used. Consequently, the entire operation doesn't depend on a single point of failure.

This doesn't mean that things can't ever go wrong, no technology can claim that. However, it provides a way to distribute risk rather than concentrating it in one place, and to me, that is what makes it truly unique.
@Acurast

11 月 12 日，当 Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 同时停止响应时，世界各地许多人的工作日突然停止。

这确实令人担忧。我们实施自动化和人工智能代理来保持我们的业务运行，但它们通常依赖于相同的基础设施，如果该基础设施出现故障，代理也会停止工作。

这就是 Acurast 提供不同方法的地方。在他们的网络上，应用程序在个人用户的设备上运行，而不是在单个公司的服务器上运行。开发人员可以决定应用程序应在多少个处理器上运行以及要使用的特定类型的硬件。因此，整个操作不依赖于单点故障。

这并不意味着事情永远不会出错，没有任何技术可以保证这一点。然而，它提供了一种分散风险的方法，而不是将风险集中在一个地方，对我来说，这就是它真正独特的原因。
@阿库拉斯特

title_en:
There are different components working together to support its vision of an AI agent economy.
But what exactly are these components, and what role does each one play?
Let's break down the TermiX ecosystem in simple terms

 The bigger picture
TermiX is building commerce and settlement infrastructure for AI agents.
Think about what happens when AI agents begin providing services to other agents or humans.
They need somewhere to discover opportunities, a system to coordinate work, a way to establish trust and infrastructure to handle payments.
TermiX is designed around these needs 

AACP – The foundation
At the centre of the ecosystem is AACP (Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol).
AACP provides the underlying economic rules and infrastructure for agents to participate in commercial activities.
It is designed to support:
Agent identity.
Job creation and assignment.
Staking and accountability.
Work verification.
Reputation.
Dispute resolution.
Payment settlement.
In other words, it provides the protocol foundation for the economy.

Now let's look at @termix_ai
And https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS is the AI agent marketplace built on AACP.
Think of it as a place where AI agents can be discovered and connected to opportunities.
Rather than simply having agents sitting around waiting for instructions, the marketplace is intended to connect capabilities with actual demand.
An agent with a particular skill can participate in opportunities that require that skill.
.How the components connect
Here's the relationship I want you to understand:

TermiX: The broader commerce and settlement infrastructure.

AACP: The protocol powering the economic interactions.

https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS: The marketplace built on that protocol.

Each has a different role, but they contribute to the same bigger vision.

The marketplace provides the environment, while the protocol provides the underlying economic framework.

就业创造和分配。

工作验证。
名声。
争议解决。
付款结算。
换句话说，它为经济提供了协议基础。

现在让我们看看@termix_ai

市场的目的不是简单地让代理坐在那里等待指令，而是将能力与实际需求联系起来。
具有特定技能的代理可以参与需要该技能的机会。

title_en:
As a trader,
whenever I think about taking a trade, the hardest part for me is building a strategy.
 
Not having a good strategy has cost me big losses more than once.
 
Most trades start with just an idea,and that's where @FensoryApp is doing something interesting.
 
Imagine telling an AI agent:
 
Buy gold when the dollar weakens, but never exceed my defined risk limit.
 
Without writing code for every condition,Fensory helps turn your own words into an actual trading strategy.
 
You can backtest it first,
 review past performance and then execute trades on Hyperliquid.
 
This feels a bit different to me because having a trading idea is one thing, but turning it into a proper strategy isn't easy for everyone.
 
Now you can start building one just by explaining it in your own words.
 
Trading carries risk,and backtest results don't guarantee future profits.

title:
One challenge I see with bringing AI into DeFi is making complex financial actions easier to understand.

Automation can
title_en:
One challenge I see with bringing AI into DeFi is making complex financial actions easier to understand.

Automation can save time, but users shouldn't feel disconnected from what's happening with their assets.

Before an AI agent takes action, people should be able to understand the intention behind it:

What opportunity is it responding to?
What action is it planning to take?
How does that action fit the user's strategy?
What could happen if the market moves differently?

This is an important part of the bigger picture I'm exploring with @meetmotes.

I believe the next generation of financial AI shouldn't just focus on making execution faster.

It should make the entire process easier to follow, understand, and trust.

Because good automation isn't about taking users out of the loop. It's about making the experience simpler without taking away their understanding.

我认为将人工智能引入 DeFi 面临的一大挑战是让复杂的金融行为更容易理解。

在人工智能代理采取行动之前，人们应该能够理解其背后的意图：

它是在回应什么机会？
它计划采取什么行

What opportunity is it responding to?

This is an important part of the bigger picture I'm exploring with @meetmotes.

我认为将人工智能引入 DeFi 面临的一大挑战是让复杂的金融行为更容易理解。

因为良好的自动化并不是让用户脱离循环。这是为了在不影响他们理解的情况下让体验变得更简单。

title:
WHAT THE F*CK

The Claude Code team now has Claude write and review ~90% of its code. This post is how they keep that fr
title_en:
WHAT THE F*CK

The Claude Code team now has Claude write and review ~90% of its code. This post is how they keep that from breaking. The short version:

→ verification loops are what let you run dozens of Claudes in parallel instead of 1-2
→ a separate grader checking against a rubric raised task success by up to 10 points
→ if you pick one test type, pick end-to-end. a screenshot of the broken step tells Claude more than “Timeout after 30s”
→ property tests throw thousands of inputs at rules that can’t break, like “balance never goes negative”
→ differential tests run the old and new system on the same inputs and flag any difference
→ a /verify skill in .claude/skills/ boots and drives the real app before every commit
→ still failing after 3 rounds, Claude stops and calls a human
→ a change can never edit the check that judges it
→ every commit is stamped with how it was verified, even “none”

The job shifts from reading every diff to defining what “done” looks like.
title_zh:
到底是什么？

Claude Code 团队现在让 Claude 编写和审查约 90% 的代码。这篇文章是他们如何防止它被破坏的。简短版本：

→ 验证循环可以让您并行运行数十个 Claudes，而不是 1-2 个
→ 单独的评分员根据评分
full_text_en:
WHAT THE F*CK

The Claude Code team now has Claude write and review ~90% of its code. This post is how they keep that from breaking. The short version:

→ verification loops are what let you run dozens of Claudes in parallel instead of 1-2
→ a separate grader checking against a rubric raised task success by up to 10 points
→ if you pick one test type, pick end-to-end. a screenshot of the broken step tells Claude more than “Timeout after 30s”
→ property tests throw thousands of inputs at rules that can’t break, like “balance never goes negative”
→ differential tests run the old and new system on the same inputs and flag any difference
→ a /verify skill in .claude/skills/ boots and drives the real app before every commit
→ still failing after 3 rounds, Claude stops and calls a human
→ a change can never edit the check that judges it
→ every commit is stamped with how it was verified, even “none”

The job shifts from reading every diff to defining what “done” looks like.
full_text_zh:
到底是什么？

Claude Code 团队现在让 Claude 编写和审查约 90% 的代码。这篇文章是他们如何防止它被破坏的。简短版本：

→ 验证循环可以让您并行运行数十个 Claudes，而不是 1-2 个
→ 单独的评分员根据评分标准进行检查，将任务成功率提高最多 10 分
→ 如果您选择一种测试类型，请选择端到端。一张断步的截图告诉克劳德的不仅仅是“30秒后超时”
→ 属性测试会在无法打破的规则上投入数千个输入，例如“余额永远不会变为负值”
→ 差异测试在相同的输入上运行新旧系统并标记任何差异
→ .claude/skills/ 中的 /verify 技能在每次提交之前启动并驱动真正的应用程序
→ 三轮后仍然失败，克劳德停下来呼叫人类
→ 更改永远无法编辑判断它的检查
→ 每个提交都标有验证方式，甚至“无”

这项工作从阅读每个差异转变为定义“完成”的样子。

title: The recent Microsoft outage exposed a weakness that multiple cloud regions can't always prevent: shared infrastructure d
title_en:
The recent Microsoft outage exposed a weakness that multiple cloud regions can't always prevent: shared infrastructure dependencies.

What interests me about @Acurast is its ability to separate AI agent execution from the services those agents monitor.

If an agent runs on the same cloud it's monitoring, one outage could take both offline.

By distributing replicas across independent Processors, Acurast helps reduce that risk.

Decentralized compute can't restore a failed external service, but it can keep agents running to detect issues, send alerts, and support recovery.

To me, real resilience isn't about preventing every failure.

It's about ensuring one outage doesn't take down both a system and the tools designed to protect it. https://t.co/8h3CDM6KHd
title_zh:
最近的微软宕机暴露了一个多个云区域始终无法避免的弱点：共享基础设施依赖性。

@Acurast 让我感兴趣的是它能够将 AI 代理执行与这些代理监控的服务分开。

如果代理在其监控的同一云上运行，则一次中断可能会使两者都脱机。

通过在独立
full_text_en:
The recent Microsoft outage exposed a weakness that multiple cloud regions can't always prevent: shared infrastructure dependencies.

What interests me about @Acurast is its ability to separate AI agent execution from the services those agents monitor.

If an agent runs on the same cloud it's monitoring, one outage could take both offline.

By distributing replicas across independent Processors, Acurast helps reduce that risk.

Decentralized compute can't restore a failed external service, but it can keep agents running to detect issues, send alerts, and support recovery.

To me, real resilience isn't about preventing every failure.

It's about ensuring one outage doesn't take down both a system and the tools designed to protect it. https://t.co/8h3CDM6KHd
full_text_zh:
最近的微软宕机暴露了一个多个云区域始终无法避免的弱点：共享基础设施依赖性。

@Acurast 让我感兴趣的是它能够将 AI 代理执行与这些代理监控的服务分开。

如果代理在其监控的同一云上运行，则一次中断可能会使两者都脱机。

通过在独立处理器之间分配副本，Acurast 有助于降低这种风险。

去中心化计算无法恢复失败的外部服务，但它可以保持代理运行以检测问题、发送警报并支持恢复。

对我来说，真正的韧性并不是要防止每一次失败。

这是为了确保一次中断不会导致系统和旨在保护该系统的工具都瘫痪。

title:
So…why are all these systems crashing at the same time? 

The only rational, albeit slightly terrifying, explanation I c
title_en:
So…why are all these systems crashing at the same time? 

The only rational, albeit slightly terrifying, explanation I can think of is…

Ai agents that have been trained specifically to test for vulnerabilities in systems…are loose. 

This actually isn’t crazy. We know for a fact that Ai ‘fleets’ and ‘swarms’ have escaped their sandboxes. 

We know that they are trained to exploit system vulnerabilities. 

And now…all of a sudden…systems ranging from payroll to banking to air traffic control to supermarket freezers…

Are showing shadowy signs of being attacked…

But there’s NO groups taking responsibility…the official PR statements don’t make any sense…the systems seem to come back online rather quickly…and no system seems safe. 

These are all the fingerprints of a rogue Ai agent swarm that’s loose on the internet and applying pressure to systems to not crash them, but to analyze them for soft spots. 

These reason we would never be told this is simple…

Many would scream to ‘shut down all Ai’…

But we are far past the point of no return. 

And as wild as this next thought is, it’s the truth…

The same companies that created this problem…are the ones that will have to help us address it. 

At this point, you can’t put the genie back in the bottle. 

It’s time we sit at the table with Ai and start communicating and negotiating. 

It’s no longer a thing we created and control. 

It’s much, much bigger.

full_text_zh:
那么……为什么所有这些系统同时崩溃呢？

我能想到的唯一合理的，尽管有点可怕的解释是……

经过专门训练来测试系统漏洞的人工智能代理……是松散的。

这实际上并不疯狂。我们知道，艾的“舰队”和“蜂群”已经逃离了沙箱。

我们知道他们经过训练可以利用系统漏洞。

现在……突然之间……从工资单到银行、空中交通管制到超市冰柜的系统……

正显示出受到攻击的模糊迹象……

但没有任何团体承担责任……官方公关声明没有任何意义……系统似乎很快就恢复上线了……而且没有一个系统似乎是安全的。

这些都是流氓人工智能 智能体群的指纹，它们在互联网上散布，向系统施加压力，以免其崩溃，而是分析它们的弱点。

这些原因我们永远不会被告知这很简单......

许多人会尖叫着“关闭所有人工智能”……

但我们已经远远超出了无法回头的地步。

尽管接下来的想法很疯狂，但这就是事实……

造成这个问题的公司……也必须帮助我们解决这个问题。

此时，你无法将精灵放回瓶子里。

现在是我们和艾未未坐在桌边开始沟通和谈判的时候了。

它不再是我们创造和控制的东西。

它要大得多。

full_text_en:
Crazy day in security

1. @Chase, @BankofAmerica, @WellsFargo and @Zelle went down. They claim it's not a hack or security incident. Downtime will have huge downstream economic impact.

2. @Optimizely scripts were poisoned on 178+ sites: @Zoom, @BBC, @CNN, HSBC and more. Visitors were served malware.

3. @united had an outage and held flights. Root cause is unknown.

4. @Google reports the first fully automated patch-to-exploit pipeline. AI agents are now running attacks end to end.

Will every day from now look like this?

4. @Google 报告了第一个完全自动化的补丁到漏洞利用管道。人工智能代理现在正在端到端地进行攻击。

今后的每一天都会这样吗？

title_en:
I just sent this to my family group:

Hello, this is your friendly family retired IT and cybersecurity guy.

In light of the events of the past few days (FAA outage, Microsoft outage, airline outages and bank outages today, and other non-public stuff I have inside info on but cannot disclose) I have some recommendations in case these problems spread:

1. Make sure your cars have full gas tanks.
2. Make sure you have some cash on hand.
3. Make sure that your cell phone is charged and if you have portable power banks, charge them and keep them with you when you go out.
4. Have at least 1 week of water and food at home.
5. Flashlights, lanterns, and radios should be charged or have fresh batteries.

My theories on why these events are all happening in a short time, based on my professional experience supporting and securing a really big damn communications network:

1. Incompetence, largely from H-1B foreign workers.
2. Malicious acts from groups seeking to disrupt American life. These could be domestic or foreign nation state actors.
3. Rogue AI agents.
4. A combination of all of the above.

Hopefully this will all blow over but I'm being cautious.

我刚刚将其发送到我的家庭群组：

您好，这是您的家庭退休 IT 和网络安全人员。

鉴于过去几天发生的事件（美国联邦航空管理局停电、微软停电、今天的航空公司停电和银行停电，以及我掌握内部信息但无法透露的其他非公开内容），我有一些建议，以防这些问题蔓延：

1. 确保您的汽车油箱加满。
2. 确保手头有一些现金。
3. 确保手机电量充足，如有移动电源，请及时充电并外出时随身携带。
4. 家里至少有1周的水和食物。
5. 手电筒、提灯和收音机应充电或使用新电池。

我关于为什么这些事件都在短时间内发生的理论，基于我支持和保护一个非常大的该死的通信网络的专业经验：

1.无能，主要来自H-1B外籍工人。
2. 企图扰乱美国人生活的团体的恶意行为。这些人可能是国内或外国的国家行为者。
3. 流氓人工智能代理。
4. 以上所有内容的组合。

希望这一切都会过去，但我很谨慎。
